english.notes:
(i) A bicycle is a carriage.
(ii) 'Street' for the purposes of this offence includes: any road, square, court, alley and thoroughfare, or public passage. The street includes the carriageway and the footways at the sides.
(iii) The offence must be committed in the street, but the annoyance may be to 'residents', meaning the occupiers of houses in the street, although they may not be in the street at the time (Mantle v Jordan 61 JP 119).
(iv) However, section 81 of the Public Health Acts (Amendment) Act 1907 extends the definition for this particular offence to also include: any place of public resort or recreation ground belonging to, or under the control of the local authority, and any unfenced ground adjoining or abutting upon any street in an urban district.
(v) See also offence wordings: H1052 and H1348.
